title: Refused building consent: low-pitched membrane roofs on a proposed house on a coastal site (Tauranga)
jurisdiction: New Zealand (MBIE Chief Executive determination; Building Act 2004; comparative only, not Alberta)
code_edition: NZ Building Code, First Schedule, Building Regulations 1992 (footnote 3); E2/AS1 and E1/AS1 figures cited; edition of the acceptable solutions not stated

facts.text: Summary describes low-pitched TPO membrane roofs, sloping inward at slopes below the E2/AS1 acceptable solution, on a proposed house; the summary calls the house three storeys.

The body describes a 2-storey detached house with a basement in a very high wind and sea-spray zone; construction is light timber frame with steel portals, concrete slabs, driven pile footings and block foundations.
Drawings call for falls of at least 1:80 to the gutter roofs (1:100 to drainage outlets); the architect advised falls would be increased to 1:66 for settlement and tolerances.
Figure 1 is a section through the length of the house (p.1); Figure 2 is a roof plan (p.3).
The membrane is a polyester-reinforced thermoplastic polyolefin (TPO); the matter is whether the roof membrane system, meaning the structure, substrate and membrane together, complies with B2 and E2.
